comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. The three Corner Relief types at the corners of a flange on four edges, with the reported rules (mitcad#2411, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#614): t = 1, r = 1, K = 0.44 (BA = 0.72 pi), Bend Relief and Corner Relief Rectangular 1 mm, a 40 x 30 Sheet Face and one Flange of tangent length 10, Inside, on its four edges (the default Corner Gap g = t). The face is cut back to [2, 38] x [2, 28] (936); each wall is mitred g/sqrt2 short of the other's inner surface on the corner's plane and runs 1 - g/sqrt2 past the inner corner J0 of the tangent lines (walls 10 (2 (36 + 2 - sqrt2) + 2 (26 + 2 - sqrt2))). With the rules relieving flange corners each corner is opened: its two bends run to each other's tangent line and meet at J0 (bends 2 x 36 + 2 x 26 = 124 mm), and the relief is measured from J0. Flat: Tear 936 + 124 BA + walls; Rectangular w removes w^2 + 2 w BA at each corner (the bends end w short of J0, the face loses a w square); Round w a disc of diameter w centred at J0, 3 pi w^2 / 16 at each corner. Folded, a bend holds 0.75 pi mm3 per mm of its length and 1.5/1.44 mm3 per mm2 of its flat. Without the rules' relief (the flag false, as designs made before) the bends end g/sqrt2 short of J0: the round ends of the bends that the report saw at each corner.
Rectangular, 1 mm: 4 (1 + 2 BA) less than Tear.
Round, 1 mm: 3 pi / 4 less than Tear.
Tear: the bends meet at each J0.
The rules without the flag's relief (designs made before): the bends end g/sqrt2 short of J0 whatever the type.
